phases.title: Item 2 — Off-day (household schoolDays) awareness across plan/schedule views, non-blocking warnings
testsFirst: features/plan/__tests__/unit/schoolDays.test.ts: isOffDay(dayIndex, schoolDays) returns correct boolean for a custom schoolDays set; returns Mon-Fri-is-school default when schoolDays is undefined; explicit case proving Saturday is NOT off when schoolDays includes Saturday (proves not hardcoded).

features/plan/__tests__/integration/WeekGrid.test.tsx: with householdProfile.schoolDays = Mon-Fri, Saturday/Sunday columns render the off-day style; with schoolDays including Saturday, Saturday renders as a normal day (not muted). Existing default-household Sat/Sun-muted assertions must still pass unchanged (regression).

features/plan/__tests__/integration/LessonTaskForm.test.tsx: setting a due date that falls on an off day shows a visible, non-blocking inline warning; setting it on a school day shows no warning; form submission succeeds either way (not blocked).

features/plan/__tests__/integration/WeekGrid.test.tsx (or a dedicated drag-and-drop test): dropping a lesson onto an off-day column succeeds (not blocked) and the resulting confirmation/success message notes the target day is an off day.
features/schedule/__tests__/integration/SchedulePage.test.tsx: the day view for a date whose weekday is an off day shows a small 'off day' indicator in the header area; a school-day date does not.
implementationSteps: Read the plan at docs/20260717-g9-timer-schedule-planner-plan.md's Item 2 section in FULL first — it contains a complete code-path audit with exact file:line references for every consumer (WeekGrid.tsx:31-33 isWeekend, WeeklyList.tsx:26-28 identical hardcoded function, LessonTaskForm.tsx date fields, WeekGrid.tsx:215-248 handleDragEnd/DroppableCell, SchedulePage.tsx). Do not re-derive this audit from scratch.

Household.schoolDays is already the confirmed, working source of truth (features/household, HouseholdSettings.tsx, household_settings key 'schoolDays') — do not add any new setting or duplicate storage.

Add features/plan/utils/schoolDays.ts exporting a shared isOffDay(dayIndex, schoolDays?: DayOfWeek[]) helper AND the Mon-Fri default as a named export, so HouseholdSettings.tsx's own default and this helper's default can both reference the same constant (per the plan's explicit risk note: do not hand-copy the Mon-Fri default in two places).

Replace WeekGrid.tsx's and WeeklyList.tsx's hardcoded isWeekend(dayIndex) (dayIndex === 0 || 6) with the new shared isOffDay helper, sourced from useHousehold().householdProfile.schoolDays (both components already sit under HouseholdProvider and already consume useHousehold() for other fields).

LessonTaskForm.tsx: add a non-blocking, dismissible inline warning (amber-toned, reusing the existing inline-message visual language already used for titleError/timeError in the same file — NOT a window.confirm or hard block) when the chosen dueDate/plannedStartDate falls on an off day per household.schoolDays.
WeekGrid.tsx handleDragEnd: extend the existing InlineSuccess 'Moved to <Day>' message to note when the target day is an off day. Do not block the drop.
SchedulePage.tsx: add a small header note when selectedDate's weekday is an off day (text label, not color-only, per accessibility standards).

Before implementing, grep features/schedule/front/components/WeekCalendarView.tsx and MonthCalendarView.tsx for any hardcoded weekend/isWeekend concept (the plan flags this as unconfirmed/not traced) — if found, fix consistently in the same phase; if not found, note that in write-back and skip.

Do not touch features/resources/server/service.ts or LessonGenerationPanel.tsx's generation logic (already correct, confirmed by the plan's audit) — optional label-only tweak there is explicitly low-priority/optional, skip unless trivial.
phases.writeBack: Record the exact export names from schoolDays.ts (so item 3's phase, which touches the same LessonTaskForm.tsx file, knows what's already there), and whether WeekCalendarView/MonthCalendarView needed the same fix or were already clean.

phases.title: Item 1 — Learning-Time: pre-fill scheduled window from lesson, client-side clock-driven auto-start/end-reminder
testsFirst: Integration test: selecting a lesson with scheduledStartTime/scheduledEndTime set (from LessonTask, G7a) auto-selects the 'Scheduled window' radio in the config panel and fills both time inputs with the lesson's values.

Integration test: selecting a lesson WITHOUT those fields set, or no lesson (ad-hoc), leaves the channel/time fields unchanged from current defaults (regression — no behavior change for existing stopwatch/timer paths).
Integration test: a pre-filled time value can still be hand-edited by the parent before starting (override is not locked).

Integration test: with a mocked 'now' past a draft scheduled session's scheduledStart, the component calls learningTimeApi.transition with {action:'start'} without a manual click, and only once (no duplicate calls across re-renders/polling ticks) — guard against double-firing.
Integration test: with a mocked 'now' before scheduledStart, the card shows a 'Starts at HH:MM' state and does NOT call transition.

Integration test: with a mocked 'now' past a running scheduled session's scheduledEnd, a visible 'time to finish' prompt renders; the existing manual Finish/outcome flow is unchanged (no silent auto-finalize).
implementationSteps: Read the plan's Item 1 section in FULL first, especially the 'What's traced vs. unknown' subsection — server-side/background auto-start (working with no browser tab open) requires cron/worker infrastructure NOT confirmed to exist in this repo and is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE. Only build the client-side, page-open-dependent version described in 'Decided design'.

No schema change, no new API routes. NowCard.tsx's existing lessonChoice onChange handler gains a lookup into openLessons to read scheduledStartTime/scheduledEndTime off the selected LessonTask and set timeChannelType/scheduledStart/scheduledEnd local state accordingly (today's date + the lesson's HH:MM, consistent with the existing 'applies to this session only, today' model).

Add a new client-side polling effect in NowCard.tsx, alongside the existing running-session ticker (same setInterval pattern already used, per the plan's audit at NowCard.tsx:190-194): when session?.status === 'draft' && session.timeChannelType === 'scheduled', compare Date.now() to session.scheduledStart and call learningTimeApi.transition(session.id, {action:'start'}) once the threshold is crossed. Use a ref (e.g. hasAutoStartedRef) to guard against double-firing across re-renders/ticks.

RISK NOTED IN PLAN — implement the bounded-window mitigation: only auto-start when 'now' is within a bounded window past scheduledStart (e.g. same calendar day), not indefinitely, so a tab left open for hours/days past a stale scheduled time doesn't surprise-start a session. Make this an explicit, named constant, not a silent assumption.
Add a new idle-but-scheduled UI state ('Starts at HH:MM') between the existing idle and running states, shown when a draft scheduled session's start time hasn't arrived yet.

Add a visible 'Time to finish [lesson]' prompt (styled consistently with existing inline prompts already in NowCard.tsx — no new modal) when wall-clock time passes a running scheduled session's scheduledEnd. This is a prompt only — do NOT auto-finalize the session; the existing manual Finish/outcome/Save flow is unchanged.
Add a small caption noting the auto-start only works while the page is open, to set honest expectations (per the plan's explicit UI-copy guidance).

Do not touch features/learning-time/server/service.ts, repository.ts, types.ts, or db/schema.ts — the plan confirms none of this needs a service-layer or schema change; transitionSession('start') already exists and does exactly what's needed, it's just being called from a timer instead of only a click.
phases.writeBack: Record the exact bounded-window constant chosen for auto-start staleness, and confirm via test that the double-fire guard works across at least 2 polling ticks.
